chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If a man rents a house for ten dirhams, dwells in two-thirds of it, and rents out the remaining third for ten dirhams, there is no problem with it. He should not rent it out for more than what he rented it for, unless he makes an improvement in it.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on sub-leasing a rented house for the same price or a higher price?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of sub-leasing (*ta'jir*) under the principle of *urf* (customary practice), allowing a tenant to sub-lease a portion for the same total rent without penalty. It establishes a key condition: the sub-lease price must not exceed the original lease price unless the tenant has made improvements (*tadil*) that justify the increase, reflecting the Shia emphasis on fairness and preventing unjust enrichment in commercial transactions.
